evidence.description: Credential retrieval suspends and then unconditionally installs the returned credentials as logged-in state.
Credential renewal likewise updates authentication state after an await without checking whether the session changed.
User information fetched asynchronously is assigned to the current profile without verifying that it still belongs to the active session.

candidates.explanation: Actor isolation does not prevent other actor methods from executing across suspension points. A retrieval or renewal started before logout can complete afterward and set isLoggedIn back to true. Similarly, a pending user-info request can restore a profile after logout or overwrite the profile of a subsequent session. These operations have no visible session-validity check before applying their results.
candidates.title: Authentication state can be overwritten by stale asynchronous operations

evidence.description: The token-reset helper clears the ordinary tokens and login flag but never clears ssoCredentials.
Successful logout uses that helper and clears the profile, leaving the cached SSO credentials untouched.
Cookie creation checks only the current login flag before consuming the cached SSO credentials.

candidates.explanation: After logout, the previous session's transfer token remains cached. A later login sets isLoggedIn to true without replacing that cache, so getSessionTokenCookie can produce a cookie containing the previous session's token before new SSO credentials are fetched. This mixes authentication material across sessions.
candidates.title: SSO credentials survive logout and can be reused by a later session

evidence.description: Local tokens and the login flag are reset only when clearCredentials returns true.
When credential clearing fails, no error is thrown if there is no web-session error and credentials cannot be renewed.

candidates.explanation: The combination of clearCredentials returning false, no session-clearing error, and canRenewCredentials returning false causes logout to return normally without resetting tokens, the profile, or isLoggedIn. Whether credentials are renewable does not establish that the actor's existing in-memory authentication state has been cleared.
candidates.title: Logout can silently succeed without clearing local authentication state

evidence.description: Logout clears the tokens, then awaits a throwing image-cache operation before clearing userProfile.

candidates.explanation: If image-cache cleanup throws, userProfile remains populated even though stored credentials and in-memory tokens have already been cleared. Logout also propagates the cache error as a failure after authentication cleanup has succeeded, leaving partially updated session state and skipping the profile-change notification.
candidates.title: Image-cache failure interrupts logout before the profile is cleared

evidence.description: A false storage result throws credentialsStorageFailed inside the same do block whose catch wraps every error as credentialsStorageError.

candidates.explanation: The explicitly thrown AuthError.credentialsStorageFailed is always caught locally and rethrown as AuthError.credentialsStorageError. Callers therefore cannot receive or distinguish the dedicated false-result error from errors thrown by the storage operation.
candidates.title: Credential-storage failure is immediately wrapped as a different error
